chunks.text: Sobol indices over 5 assumptions for Liability with a safe harbour, shares with interactions and their 90% intervals: Safety elasticity of incidents: 54% of the value's variance (39% to 76%) and 60% of the margin's (43% to 82%). Capability growth: 45% of the value's variance (27% to 83%) and 39% of the margin's (25% to 66%). Monthly catastrophe probability: 29% of the value's variance (7% to 51%) and 32% of the margin's (7% to 56%). Trust sensitivity to harm: 19% of the value's variance (12% to 31%) and 15% of the margin's (9% to 24%). Median harm of a catastrophe: 5% of the value's variance (3% to 7%) and 5% of the margin's (3% to 8%). The intervals are wide: the design ranks groups of assumptions and does not order neighbours. Saltelli's design on scrambled Sobol points; first order by Saltelli (2010), total order by Jansen (1999); 90% bootstrap intervals over the base sample; the other assumptions are held at the run's values, so the shares are of the variance these inputs produce, and the inputs are drawn independently, as the decomposition requires.

chunks.title: Structural variants
chunks.text: Liability with a safe harbour remains the decision in 3 of 8 variants and stays within the constraints and above the status quo in 4. Myopic firms (firms plan six months ahead instead of twelve): decision Liability with a safe harbour, focus rank 1, within the constraints. Forward looking firms (firms plan two years ahead): decision Transparency and disclosure, focus rank 1, outside the constraints. Weak regulator (the regulator has half the stated capacity): decision Transparency and disclosure, focus rank 1, outside the constraints. Strong safety effect (safety practice cuts incidents faster): decision Compute threshold reporting, focus rank 2, within the constraints. Weak safety effect (safety practice cuts incidents more slowly): decision Mandatory third party evaluation, focus rank 1, outside the constraints. Lax offshore (offshore activity is twice as hazardous as at home): decision Liability with a safe harbour, focus rank 1, within the constraints. Heavy tail (the catastrophic tail is two and a half times more likely): decision Mandatory third party evaluation, focus rank 1, outside the constraints. Systemic catastrophes (catastrophic failures are strongly correlated across firms): decision Liability with a safe harbour, focus rank 1, within the constraints.

chunks.title: Evidence examined and set aside
chunks.text: Meta analysis of trust and intention to use a technology: r = 0.503 (95% interval 0.470 to 0.535, 128 samples, 50,667 respondents): not used because it supports the sign of the trust channel and nothing more: a correlation between stated attitudes in studies of online shopping, banking and e-health is not an elasticity of realised adoption to trust, and cannot be turned into one without the dispersion of both. The elasticity stays unidentified. The size of the fall in trust after a salient incident (AAA: afraid to ride rose from 63% to 73% after two fatal crashes): not used because the model moves trust with monetised harm, and two deaths are a small monetised harm: an incident of that size moves the model's trust by less than a tenth of a percent. The episode says trust answers to salience; the model's form cannot show that. Recorded as a limit of the mechanism, not scored, because the survey question is about using a vehicle. Estimates of AI's effect on output: total factor productivity up by no more than 0.66% over ten years (Acemoglu); 7% of global GDP over ten years (Goldman Sachs); $2.6 to $4.4 trillion a year (McKinsey): not used because the model declares its benefit bases in $bn a year and declares no size for the jurisdiction's economy, so there is nothing to divide by; and the estimates span an order of magnitude. Elicited probabilities of catastrophic harm from AI: not used because elicitations, not observations; they define catastrophe differently from the model and have no validation record. A loss distribution for AI incidents: not used because none has been published: the taxonomies exist, the magnitudes are not recorded. GDPR and venture investment: monthly EU deals down 26.1% against US ventures: not used because the model has no entry or investment margin to compare it with.

chunks.title: Validation and evidence
chunks.text: The Lab is synthetic: its figures are conditional on the model and its assumptions and are not validated forecasts. The model was confronted with 11 published benchmarks that bear on 10 of its 15 mechanisms. 3 of those mechanisms have a benchmark measured on AI itself; the others rest on analogues from other regulation and other technologies, each compared with an allowance for that distance. At the central assumptions the model is not contradicted by 9, is in tension with 1 (Share of the insurance loading used up by underwriting and administration) and is contradicted by 1 (Equity return when a horizontal regime becomes enforceable). Even the closest tenth of the draws of the assumptions miss Equity return when a horizontal regime becomes enforceable by more than 2 standard deviations: that is a failure of the model's form and not of a parameter value, so it is reported and left out of the weighting below. No benchmark bears on 5 mechanisms: severity, catastrophic tail, safety practice, evaluation, news. Weighting the 64 joint draws of the assumptions by how well each reproduces the 10 benchmarks it can be compared with leaves an effective 27 draws. In the weighted draws the decision is Transparency and disclosure in 39% (unweighted 36%); Mandatory third party evaluation in 32% (unweighted 22%); Liability with a safe harbour in 29% (unweighted 39%); Compute threshold reporting in 0% (unweighted 2%). 92% of the draws are ruled out by no benchmark at 3 standard deviations. Liability with a safe harbour is within the constraints and above the status quo in 36% of the weighted draws (42% unweighted). The benchmarks bear on 13 of the 68 assumptions drawn; they move most Resource share of the insurance loading (+0.7 sd), Price jump on an own incident (-0.3 sd), Capability growth (-0.2 sd), Audit rate (+0.1 sd), Revenue response to capability (-0.1 sd). Weighting by benchmarks is a posterior given the allowances declared for each benchmark, not a measurement: most of the evidence is an analogue, and a wide allowance makes a benchmark easy to pass and uninformative. What the benchmarks do not reach is listed with the reasons; in particular nothing here identifies the elasticity of realised adoption to trust. No price series of an observed event was uploaded on this run. No mechanism is estimated from data; 10 of 15 were confronted with a published benchmark.

chunks.title: Mechanism register
chunks.text: Reportable incidents arrive at a rate that rises with released capability and deployment reach and falls with safety practice: uncalibrated; test: Held out incident counts per firm and year inside the model's predictive interval; the sign and size of the safety elasticity from before and after comparisons at firms that adopt evaluation regimes. The monetised harm of an incident is lognormal with a heavy tail; an incident at or above a threshold is major: uncalibrated; test: The empirical tail of documented losses against the lognormal fit; the share of incidents above the major threshold. Above a critical capability a firm faces a small monthly probability of a catastrophic incident, reduced by safety practice and evaluation, and correlated across firms: uncalibrated, untestable ex ante; test: Not testable before the event. Treated by sensitivity: both ends of every range in the screen, the joint draw, and the heavy tail and systemic variants. Near miss frequencies would be partial evidence on the prior. The share of R&D spent on safety raises safety practice with diminishing returns and displaces part of capability growth; practice decays without investment: uncalibrated; test: Firm level safety budgets against evaluation pass rates and incident rates over time. A mandated evaluation catches a share of unsafe releases before deployment: uncalibrated; test: Post mortems of incidents: the share traceable to failures an evaluation at release would have found. Each month a firm chooses its safety share, offshore share and whether to comply by maximising a one year expected payoff under its own optimistic view of incident risk: uncalibrated; test: Observed compliance rates, safety budgets and release cadence after an instrument takes effect, against the model's. Firms move activity offshore when the instrument binds at home; moved activity is laxer, loses revenue and takes domestic rents with it: uncalibrated; test: Changes in establishment location, hiring and model release geography around regulatory dates, against unaffected sectors. Capability grows with R&D; licensing delays releases; a moratorium freezes released capability and slows research in scope; published weights diffuse capability: uncalibrated; test: Release cadence and benchmark trajectories before and after a licensing regime. Reach closes on a ceiling set by released capability and public trust; trust falls with harm and recovers slowly; adoption benefits scale with trust: uncalibrated; test: Survey trust and adoption series around salient incidents. A firm's revenue grows at a rate that fades from its starting pace towards a long run rate, moves with released capability and reach, and for chip and cloud firms with the developers' growth: uncalibrated; test: Revenue growth of listed AI firms against capability releases and adoption series. Enforcement intensity follows news pressure within the regulator's capacity; audits find the non compliant and fine them: uncalibrated; test: Enforcement actions against news attention series for an existing regulator. Incidents, enforcement, relocations and releases become a news pressure index with memory, and a wire of headlines on the representative path: uncalibrated; test: Forecast coverage counts for a policy domain against observed counts. A firm's price is a fundamental value (revenue and forward earnings multiples) times a sentiment component driven by the market factor, news pressure, incident jumps and, for an instrument announced before it takes effect, an anticipation term: partly calibrable; one mechanism testable here; test: Implemented: an event study on an uploaded series mapped to a firm and an instrument, against the model's predictive distribution of the early reaction; with eight or more mapped events, the coverage of the 10th to 90th percentile band. Consumer surplus and the output uplift are powers of the AI service index around declared annual bases: declared value judgements; test: Not a testable mechanism: a valuation. Treated by sensitivity. Liability moves a share of harm to the firm in scope; a safe harbour shields the compliant; a mandate replaces realised liability with a premium loaded above expected claims: uncalibrated; test: Quoted premiums and exclusions for AI liability cover against the model's.

chunks.title: Instruments
chunks.text: Status quo (voluntary commitments): No new obligation. Existing consumer and product law only, with the regulator's present capacity. Every other policy is measured against this path, pair by pair. Compute threshold reporting: Developers above a training compute threshold report their models and their own evaluations. The regime an executive order can create. Frontier licensing: A licence to train or deploy above the capability threshold: mandated safety spend, independent evaluation, an approval delay, audits with real fines. Domestic scope: a mobile lab can leave. Liability with a safe harbour: Strict liability, but a firm that meets the evaluation and safety spend standard is shielded from most of it. Compliance becomes the cheaper choice. Mandatory third party evaluation: Independent pre deployment evaluation above a threshold, with a short approval delay. Catches a share of unsafe releases before they ship. Six month moratorium above the threshold: Releases above the capability threshold are frozen for six months, then reporting applies. The sharpest brake and the one most easily left behind. Risk tiering (EU style): Obligations by use case tier for every deployer, conformity assessment before high risk deployment, a sandbox for small firms. Compliance cost scales with deployment, not with the frontier. Strict liability: Firms pay for the harm their systems cause, insured by mandate. No ex ante obligation: the price of an incident does the work, and the firms choose their own safety spend. Transparency and disclosure: Model documentation, provenance marking and public incident disclosure. Cheap, and it shrinks the misuse environment rather than the capability.
